[SS 11/2 | Lesson Title] Unit 2: Let’s Go Exploring
[SS 11/2 | GaDOE Inspire] Early Explorer Trading Cards
[SS 11/2 | Standard] SS3H2 Describe European exploration in North America.
[SS 11/2 | Learning Target] I can research six explorers, identify where and when they explored, describe their achievements and character traits, and use evidence to compare their experiences and historical impact.
[SS 11/2 | Five-Day Teaching Sequence, Tuesday] Research & gather facts: Read across leveled sources; begin research organizer and cards for John Cabot, Vasco Núñez de Balboa, and Hernando de Soto.
[SS 11/2 | Hook & Video Exploration] What challenges might explorers have faced, and how might people already living in these places have experienced their arrival?
[SS 11/9 | Date(s)] November 9-13th
[SS 11/9 | Lesson Title] Unit 3: Let’s Go Exploring
[SS 11/9 | GaDOE Inspire] Economic Choices for Early Explorers
[SS 11/9 | Additional Resources] Read Aloud: Vasco Núñez de Balboa
[SS 11/9 | Five-Day Teaching Sequence, Monday] Monday, Nov. 9: Launch: review exploration and cause/effect. Introduce scarcity, beliefs, values, and opportunity cost with a simple classroom choice.
[SS 11/9 | Five-Day Teaching Sequence, Thursday] Thursday, Nov. 12: Investigate achievements: verify actual achievements and costs using biographies, encyclopedias, and appropriate websites. Complete group portion of Economic Choices Table; prepare spokesperson.
[SS 11/9 | Retrieval Activator] Why did explorers travel? What resources did they need?
[SS 11/9 | Retrieval Activator] Present a choice: “You have one hour—study or play. What is the opportunity cost?”
[SS 11/9 | Guided Discovery] Explicitly define scarcity (not enough resources for every want) and opportunity cost (the next-best alternative given up).
[SS 11/9 | Guided Discovery] Assign one of six explorers per group: John Cabot, Vasco Núñez de Balboa, Hernando de Soto, Christopher Columbus, Henry Hudson, or Jacques Cartier.
[SS 11/9 | Stations] Values & Beliefs: Sort desire/value cards; discuss why each goal may have mattered to the explorer and sponsor
[SS 11/9 | Vocabulary] Core: scarcity, desire, value, belief, opportunity cost, decision, achievement, evidence, inference, explorer, expedition, voyage.
[ELA 11/9 | Date(s), Title] November 9-13 · Unit 3: Another View Session 6-10
[ELA 11/9 | Graphic Organizer] 11/9 – Compare and Contrast Maybe Maybe and Surely Surely Venn Diagram. Students compare the characters, setting, problems, solutions, and lessons learned in both stories.
[ELA 11/9 | Graphic Organizer] 11/10 - Narrative Ending Planner. Students use this organizer to plan a different ending for the story about Leo and the school play.
[ELA 11/9 | Retrieval Activator] 11/11 Do Now Session 8 Pg. 79 - Assessment & Collaborative Discussion
[ELA 11/9 | Formative Assessment] Write a new ending for Leo's story that solves his problem and makes sense with the earlier events.
[M 11/9 | Lesson] Lesson 13 - Understand Patterns
[M 11/9 | Standard] 3.PAR.3.1 Describe, extend, and create numeric patterns related to multiplication. Make predictions related to the patterns.
[M 11/30 | Date(s), Lesson] November 30- December 4, 2026 · Lesson 16 - Add Areas
[M 11/30 | Standard] 3.GSR.7.2 Determine the area of rectangles (or shapes composed of rectangles) presented in relevant problems by tiling and counting.
[M 12/7 | Date(s), Lesson] December 7-11, 2026 · Lesson 32 - Area and Perimeter of Shapes
[M 12/7 | Standard] 3.GSR.8.1 Determine the perimeter of a polygon and explain that the perimeter represents the distance around a polygon. Solve problems involving perimeters of polygons.
[M 12/7 | Standard] 3.GSR.8.2 Investigate and describe how rectangles with the same perimeter can have different areas or how rectangles with the same area can have different perimeters.
